description_full: Teradata Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides an AI and knowledge platforms in the United States and internationally. It operates in two segments, Product Sales and Consulting Services. The company's AI and Knowledge platform designed for enterprise-grade workloads. Its consulting services include support services for organizations to establish data analytics and AI vision, enable a hybrid ecosystem architecture, and identify and operationalize opportunities. The company serves clients in financial services, healthcare and life sciences, public sector, manufacturing, retail, telecommunications, and travel/transportation sectors through a direct sales force. Teradata Corporation was incorporated in 1979 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 5K people. Revenue per employee of $326K ranks in the below the sector median among Technology peers. Each employee generates $56K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $22K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 6× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: Teradata Corporation is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.0B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years and -4% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 59% against a 9% cost of capital — a 50-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 56% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $286M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -9.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 7.9×.

Shareholder yield of 4.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $37.0M (1% of market cap).

The current ratio of 0.92 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -2.5% over 3 years, -2.0% over 5 years and -4.1% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 22% of profits supports about 13.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.

Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.93 (orders lagging sales), a backlog worth 1.3x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 4%.
Capex runs only 0.2x depreciation (1.1% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 9, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (1.0%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).

It returns 4.7% a year to shareholders (4.7% in buybacks).

Short interest is elevated at 22.7% of the float, 9.1 days to cover.
people: With about 5,100 employees, each generates about $326K of revenue, in line with the Technology median.
